title: Nabla vs Mentalyc: AI Scribe Comparison for Mental Health (2026)
description: Compare Nabla and Mentalyc for therapy documentation. Nabla is enterprise-grade for health systems; Mentalyc is built specifically for therapists with modality-aware AI. See pricing, features, and which fits your practice.

summary.bottom_line: Mentalyc is purpose-built for therapists with modality-aware AI (CBT, DBT, EMDR) and Alliance Genie therapeutic tracking. Nabla is an enterprise ambient scribe for health systems and multi-specialty practices-it doesn't understand therapy modalities. Therapists doing psychotherapy should choose Mentalyc. Psychiatrists doing medication management in large health systems might consider Nabla.

sections.heading: Nabla vs Mentalyc: Overview
sections.content: Nabla and Mentalyc serve fundamentally different markets. Nabla is an enterprise ambient AI scribe designed for hospitals and multi-specialty health systems, serving 85,000+ clinicians across 150+ organizations in 35+ languages. Mentalyc was built exclusively for therapists and mental health professionals, understanding therapy modalities (CBT, DBT, EMDR, psychodynamic) and generating therapy-specific documentation. While Nabla has mental health templates, they lack specialty depth. Therapists doing psychotherapy should use Mentalyc.

sections.heading: Mental Health Documentation
sections.content: Mentalyc's core differentiator is therapy modality awareness. It understands how CBT sessions differ from DBT, EMDR, or psychodynamic therapy and generates notes that reflect the actual therapeutic approach. Mentalyc's Alliance Genie tracks therapeutic relationship dynamics with data-driven insights-a capability no other scribe offers. Nabla's mental health templates are basic: they may lack all MSE domains, structured risk assessment fields, and don't understand therapy modalities. Nabla works for psychiatrists doing routine medication management, but therapists need Mentalyc.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Mentalyc has transparent pricing: Mini at $19.99/month (10 notes), Basic at $39.99/month (50 notes), Pro at $69.99/month (160 notes), Super at $119.99/month (330 notes), and Group Practice at $49.99-59.99/seat with unlimited notes. Nabla doesn't publish pricing since 2026-reported rates are ~$119/month for individuals and $299-399/provider for enterprise. Nabla has a free tier (30 encounters) but BAA availability is unclear, creating HIPAA compliance concerns for clinical use.

sections.heading: EHR Integrations
sections.content: Nabla integrates with large health system EHRs: Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, NextGen, Greenway, Altera, and MEDITECH. Mentalyc integrates with mental health-specific platforms: TherapyNotes, ICANotes, TheraNest, Valant, and SimplePractice (via Chrome extension). The integration landscape reflects each tool's target market. If you use a mental health EHR, Mentalyc likely has better integration.

sections.heading: Privacy and Compliance
sections.content: Nabla's key privacy feature is zero server-side storage-patient audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. Mentalyc is SOC 2 Type II certified and deletes audio after note generation. Both are HIPAA compliant, but Nabla's free tier may not include a BAA (unconfirmed), which is a compliance gap. Mentalyc includes BAA on all plans.

recommendations.when: You're a therapist doing psychotherapy and need modality-aware documentation (CBT, DBT, EMDR); you want Alliance Genie therapeutic relationship tracking; you use mental health EHRs like TherapyNotes, TheraNest, or Valant; or you want transparent pricing without a sales conversation

You work in a large health system with Epic or Cerner; you're a psychiatrist doing medication management (not psychotherapy); you need 35+ language support for diverse patient populations; or your organization already has Nabla deployed
You want the cheapest option (AutoNotes at $24/month) or you want session analytics (Upheal offers talk-time and sentiment tracking that neither Nabla nor Mentalyc provides)

faqs.q: Is Nabla or Mentalyc better for therapists?
faqs.a: Mentalyc is significantly better for therapists. It was built specifically for mental health and understands therapy modalities (CBT, DBT, EMDR, psychodynamic). Nabla was designed for health systems and multi-specialty practices-it doesn't understand therapy or generate modality-aware notes.

faqs.q: Does Nabla understand therapy modalities like CBT or DBT?
faqs.a: No. Nabla is a general-purpose medical scribe that doesn't understand therapy modalities. Its mental health templates are basic and may lack MSE domains and structured risk assessment fields. Use Mentalyc for therapy-specific documentation.

faqs.q: How much does Nabla cost compared to Mentalyc?
faqs.a: Mentalyc is cheaper and more transparent: $19.99-119.99/month depending on plan. Nabla doesn't publish pricing-reported rates are ~$119/month for individuals and $299-399/provider for enterprise contracts. Nabla requires a sales conversation.

Alliance Genie is Mentalyc's unique feature that tracks therapeutic alliance dynamics with data-driven insights into the therapist-client relationship. No other AI scribe, including Nabla, offers this therapeutic relationship tracking capability.

faqs.q: Does Nabla's free tier include a BAA?
faqs.a: BAA availability on Nabla's free tier is not confirmed. Using an AI scribe on patient encounters without a BAA is a HIPAA compliance gap. Verify with Nabla before clinical use. Mentalyc includes BAA on all plans.
